data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise nuanced modal and semi-modal meanings including obligation, deduction, criticism, past possibility and expectation.
learningPoints: Use must have, might have and can't have for past deduction.
Use should have for criticism or regret about the past.
Distinguish mustn't from don't have to and needn't.
Use ought to and be supposed to for expectation and advice.
Use needn't have to describe unnecessary completed actions.
Choose modal meaning according to certainty, obligation and hindsight.

sections.explain: MUST HAVE + past participle expresses a strong deduction about the past.

words.word: She must have forgotten the meeting.
She must forgot the meeting.
She must to have forgotten the meeting.

sections.summary: Using 'can't have' for impossible past deduction.
sections.explain: CAN'T HAVE + past participle expresses strong belief that something did not happen.

words.word: He can't have seen the message; his phone was off.
He mustn't have seen the message; his phone was off, meaning deduction.
He can't has seen the message; his phone was off.

sections.summary: Using 'might have' for uncertain past possibility.
sections.explain: MIGHT HAVE + past participle expresses a possible past event.

words.word: They might have taken the wrong train.
They might took the wrong train.
They might to have taken the wrong train.

sections.explain: SHOULD HAVE + past participle can express criticism or regret about an earlier action.

words.word: You should have told me earlier.
You should told me earlier.
You should have tell me earlier.

sections.explain: MUSTN'T means prohibited; DON'T HAVE TO means not necessary.

words.word: You don't have to come if you're busy.
You mustn't come if you're busy, meaning it is optional.
You don't must come if you're busy.

sections.explain: NEEDN'T HAVE + past participle means an action was done but was unnecessary.

words.word: You needn't have bought any food; we had plenty.
You didn't need buy any food, so you definitely bought it unnecessarily.
You needn't have buy any food.

sections.explain: OUGHT TO expresses advice, expectation or moral obligation.

words.word: You ought to apologise.
You ought apologise.
You ought to apologising.

sections.explain: BE SUPPOSED TO expresses expectation, arrangement or rule.

words.word: We're supposed to be there by nine.
We're suppose to be there by nine.
We're supposed being there by nine.

sections.summary: Using 'could have' for unrealised past possibility.
sections.explain: COULD HAVE + past participle can express something that was possible but did not happen.

words.word: We could have taken a taxi, but we decided to walk.
We could took a taxi, but we decided to walk.
We could have take a taxi, but we decided to walk.

sections.explain: Different modal perfect forms express deduction, possibility, criticism or unrealised possibility.

words.word: He may have misunderstood what you meant.
He may misunderstood what you meant.
He may to have misunderstood what you meant.
